notes.title: Warlordocracy Early Access v5.5 and v5.6
notes.content:
This should be the final patch before I keep working on the story. The AI can now use abilities (berserk, power slash, defensive stance, disarming, mad dash, etc.). There is also an AI setting in the journal settings to allow your party members to use items and abilities on their own (set to "advanced").

Added lots of text to the World Atlas PDF. I was gonna pull a Gollum and sell it as a $5 "Lore Pack" DLC, but decided that was stupid.

Also, I still haven't resubmitted Brigand to GOG because I made a couple updates recently. I will eventually get around to it after Summer sales (get me some more reviews first).

[b]Complete List of Changes:[/b]

Version 5.6:

-Changed Bonecraft ability to Wizardry (not in Ch.1).
-Beating a chapter now displays number of game days passed.
-Human, krug, trog, and siliki death scripts now have 50% chance to drop 1 coin.
-Improved random map generator, wood bridges now generated when roads cross rivers.
-You can no longer throw objects at normal objects that block movement and/or sight (like walls).
-Now only party members take damage if attacking unarmed (so animals don't hurt themselves attacking).
-Fixed script bug where "attPoison.wsl" and "attDiseased.wsl" scripts would affect plants, undead, etc.
-Added commands: "partyDelete" and "partyInvDelete" to help with importing parties in the future.
-Added command: "objUseAbility" for mobiles to use given ability at current target.
-Added script boolean: "if_objNearFriend" to test if mobile of same faction is within given range.
-Added script boolean: "if_partyAI" to test Party AI setting in scripts (0 to 2).
-"UseItems.wsl" script now allows party members to use items if Party AI is set to 2.
-"UseItems.wsl" script now allows mobiles to use combat abilities (party members if AI is set to 2).
-Moved Feluco to the entrance of the Bandit Camp so dialogue is automatic.
-Replaced iron fence in Tuskwood with iron gate (bigger, less confusing).
-Added sound effects for plant attacks (mantraps and shamblers).
-Added descriptions to the World Atlas, updated all PDF manuals.
-Replaced "Victory.ogg" track.

Version 5.5:

-Thrown items now deal bonus damage based on Physique skill.
-Time now advances every 4 seconds instead of 3 (day/night cycle now longer).
-Transition scripts now pass the time, and inform the player of how many hours the trip takes.
-Added new script command: "timePass" to have given amount of hours pass (1 game hour = 100 real seconds).
-Weather change is now done in "climate" scripts, which are broken down into different climates.
-Changing the weather no longer calls the map script automatically (prevents infinite loop).
-Fixed bug where no inventory room message would appear multiple times after quantity input.
-Fixed script bugs with butterflies reappearing in the morning.

notes.title: Version 11.8
notes.content:
You can now click around on different teammates and equipment in the character info screen (see video below). Also, Ramirez can now train you up to 50 Agility (there was no master Agility trainer before). Some other minor bug fixes. Final update of all time.

Complete list of changes:

SOURCE CODE:
-You can now change teammates and equipment in the Character Info screen with the mouse.
-Fixed bug where "resetStats" and "resetVars" wouldn't work when called in other scripts.
-Fixed bug where you would use yourself if pressing SHIFT while attacking with melee weapons.
-Made max Meta requirements more clear when unlocking abilities.

SCRIPTS:
-Ramirez INIT script now has 50 Agility (for training).
-(PANAMA) Made Hutch immune to bullets before Chapter 4.
-(PANAMA) Changed objective text in SQUIRREL story to accomodate players who didn't talk to Whooper.

STORY FILES: (requires starting a new game)
-Ramirez now has 50 Agility in story file for OAXACA and NIGHTMARE.

notes.title: Warlordocracy Early Access v5.3 and v5.4
notes.content:
Two more Warlordocracy updates I'm posting here. AI has been improved further, the game now asks how many items you want to get if there's more than 1, and lots of bug fixing and game balancing. Will be leaving early access in August. Gonna take a vacation for a few days then come back and crunchy crunch.

Also, finished a second map for the Patreon Stories DLC, which you can get here: [url=https://www.patreon.com/posts/83271359]https://www.patreon.com/posts/83271359[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29239340/e0fbe3bb937ab969609a7756afc5f20b7e884401.png[/img]

Version 5.3

-Improved pathfinding a bit more.
-Added script for Pickpocket ability (not in Ch.1).
-Plates and vases can now be used to throw at targets like stones.
-Random map generator now prevents roads and rivers from overlapping.
-Red targeting visual highlights when using abilities, items, etc. now factors in line of sight.
-Player can now input amount when getting an item if there are multiple items of the same name in the tile.

Just don't redist the EXEs so they have to download this first, and also put the laughingcoyote.net link in there. Then sell them bitches.

I gotta focus on Warlordocracy for now.

notes.title: Future Plans for Warlordocracy

LINK: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1748160/Warlordocracy/]https://store.steampowered.com/app/1748160/Warlordocracy/[/url]

I am still working on another couple of side-quests in the Warlordocracy demo and finalizing the class balance (gotta add in some bluff dialogue options, etc.). Then I'm gonna playtest through the demo with every class, then hopefully update on Fuck Napoleon III day, March 5th.

The demo is going to stay restricted to only 10 maps, so I'm done with the demo maps. I just need to make sure that the classes are balanced, finish some more dialogue and side-quests, and hopefully improve the pathfinding a lot more. Then I can keep working on the full version.

You can import your entire party and list of reputations into different stories with the script commands already, so I think the first full paid release will be the first four chapters. There will be a satisfying conclusion but obviously some loose ends. Then there will be a couple DLCs that add two more chapters each that you can import your party and reputations into. So there will probably be a total of 8 chapters before the party gets too overpowered. I have tons of story notes and an ultimate ending, and now I just need a way to conclude the base game in a satisfactory way before the optional expansions.

There, I made the outline of my outline. Time to get high.

notes.title: Command Prompt Fix for Old Saves
notes.content:
Sorry, I renamed all 10mm and 6mm Clips to 10mm and 6mm Mags because tons of gun nerds play this shit that I wanna kung fu the shit out of. So that means if you're loading an old save and you buy new ammo, it won't stack with your old ammo in the inventory. Here's how to fix it:

1) Turn on world editor mode in the launcher and load your save.
2) Press F2, left click the mouse to open the command prompt.
3) Type "renameAll=10mm Clip,10mm Mag" and press ENTER (comma between parameters).
4) Then type "renameAll=6mm Clip,6mm Mag" and press ENTER.
5) Leave blank and press ENTER again, then press ESC to leave the world editor
6) Save your game, then quit the game.
7) Relaunch with world editor mode turned off again so you can get Steam achievements.

notes.title: Brigand: Panama DLC is Working
notes.content:
Two weeks after the expected launch date, Brigand: Panama is up on Steam. There will probably be a couple of logistical script bugs because I do not want to limit player freedom, and there's always something people do on Youtube videos or Steam discussions that I would never have thought of.

Panama is an entirely new story with a new player character -- it doesn't change the original story at all, so start a new game and select the "Brigand - Panama" story.

It's about half the length of Oaxaca, but it's hard right from the beginning. Also, there are lots of new features, such as a woodcraft ability that lets you craft bamboo into throwing spears, smoking pipes, and fishing rods. There are also traps. A whole poopoo platter of traps. And a lot more items, baddies, and characters. There will be an update next weekend for sure.

Thanks to the Steam Team for being patient with my dumb ass.

Also, thanks to MAAU for the serious shout-out, even though I don't understand a word of it:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ixllzrRFENU

It's $4.99, but you'll get all future updates on itch.io if you get it there. I need playtesters before I put it on Steam with achievements, voice acting, etc. Since I have no money, I would like to offer a deal: you report one bug that I have never heard of before, I will give you one free Steam key when it's out as long as it's a bug I was previously unaware of. You find 5 bugs, I'll give you 5 Steam keys (5 max). Give them out for bullshit anniversary gifts to make your neighbor play it and ignore his wife, then you can swoop in.

I wish I could have done this when Oaxaca came out, but the only reason people knew about my shit was because of Steam. Catch-22 is a bitch.

notes.content:
Two or three people have complained that recent versions run more slowly (also I have to say "more slowly" because I'm a fucking English teacher unfortunately).

I forgot that about 2 or 3 months ago I changed the main game loop from the usual do/loop loop to a for/next loop in which I reset the variable at the end every time. I got this advice from the DBP forums saying it was a problem in the C++ source code, and sure enough it squeezed another 2-3 FPS on both my old-ass computers.

However, it just donged on me that this may not be the case for newer computers. Hence, I want to provide a link to a new exe called "Brigand Test.exe". notes.title: Version 4.9
notes.content:
Next version is up. There are now 3 team orders: Regroup (team follows selected player), Defend (team does not follow), and Hold (team does not move whatsoever, but they still attack).

As for the accuracy balance, I just gave the currently-selected player +5 bonus to aim, nobody else. Scope zooming no longer gives a bonus to accuracy, as the magnification is bonus enough.

Another important fix is that I finally fixed that bug reported by multiple people where your party would leave and be replaced by "?" icons when you return to the plantation in Ch. 5.

Complete list of changes is below.

SOURCE CODE:
-Increased default firearm accuracy slightly (for currently-selected player only).
-Removed aiming bonus from scope zooming to compensate (magnification should be enough benefit).

-Fixed bug where "if_inParty" script boolean wouldn't work when moving to a new map (fixing Ch. 5 bug when returning to plantation).

-You can now sacrifice 50 jink at voodoo altars (instead of 100).
-Fixed bug where workers would not sell you yucca fruit.

-Update Player's Manual and Builder's Manual.

notes.title: Version 4.3
notes.content:
New patch. The main thing is that it delays characters for 0.6 seconds after a close-up dialogue with them. That way they can't murder you immediately after the conversation ends (this was especially a problem with laser weapons).

I have also added an Exclusive Mode option in the launcher app, which makes the resolution a little crisper, but the game will crash if you minimize it in Exclusive Mode. I'm hoping this option might fix some compatibility issues.

There's a lot of other fixes based on recent bug reports. Fucking thank you everybody for reporting bugs.

Here's a complete list of fixes:

SOURCE CODE:
-Delayed characters from attacking 0.6 seconds after a close-up dialogue window.
-Added new option to launch in Exclusive Mode (resolution is crisper, but you can't minimize).
-Fixed bug related to giving a character an item when inventory is full ("copy" command would not work with dropped items).
-Fixed problem with "regroupTeam" script command.

SCRIPTS:
-Improved Recruit Soldiers ability: added choice window and made it cheaper.
-Updated Laughing Coyote's ability upgrades between chapters to the new ability names.
-Modified AI for BRIGAND - FORTRESS to keep the 2 mercs outside the temple from running off.
-Made all teammates leave in the Pochutla Sewers for AI purposes (instead of only main characters).
-Fixed a bug with McVannon's Plot job, where you can report to Uncle Bob after reading MV's Journal.
-Other minor script error fixes.

STORY FILE: (requires starting a new game)
-Changed names of 2 mercs in BRIGAND - FORTRESS to "Merc Guards" (for AI purposes).

notes.title: Panama Plans
notes.content:
I haven't had much time to work on Panama because I've been sleeping about 3 hours per night. Anywho, I'm quitting my evening class after New Years so I can finish this fucking storyline.

I got good shit planned, but Panama may not come out until March (at the latest). I wanna make the ending of this story not suck.

notes.title: Version 4.2 + Steam Achievements
notes.content:
Version 4.2 is up, which includes 50 Steam achievements. Please let me know if anything is slower due to the plugin I am using. I don't think there should be any problems. By the way, if you are playing in editor mode, you can't unlock achievements.

I'm gonna release v4.2B tomorrow with a couple other improvements.

EDIT: Alright, version 4.2B is out. You can look at the updates text file for a full list of changes. Now I'm going to the bar to drink and grade tests.

notes.title: Version 4.1B and Future Plans
notes.content:
Damaging property used to have no negative effect because I didn't give factions to wooden doors, crates, etc. If I had, smashing a crate would have had the same consequences as stabbing someone to death. Oops.

Now property destruction will only decrease respect by 5% instead of 20%, and I went around the story file giving factions to lots of doors and crates. This means you have to start a new story file for the doors, etc. to have factions. I also made it so that you will only lose respect if someone sees you (like stealing).

Finally, I made the little wall outside the Pochutla Market near Leon taller and moved the cooking fire away. You used to be able to jump over that and skip to Chapter 3.


FUTURE PLANS:

Version 4.2 won't be out for a while, but I plan to address the performance problems and the memory crash problems that some people are having. It might be due to Windows 10, not sure.

I'm gonna try to release Brigand: Panama by New Years. I've got half the maps finished, as well as lots of the new items, baddies, abilities, etc. You can use bamboo to make throwing spears, smoking pipes, and fishing rods. There are also flamethrowers, homing rockets, bear traps, prox mines, other traps, new herbs, clams, and more.

Unfortunately, I have only just started on the actual character scripts and dialogue.

notes.content:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RjMQ2q_nsh8

Also thanks to 14pat and Gruppy for the bug reports. There are lots of important fixes, so I'll just give you the complete list:

SOURCE CODE:
-Dialogue close-ups no longer change player direction.
-Fixed a bug where ambient sounds would constantly restart.
-Increased climbing limit for polycollision objects, fixing problem with guard tower ramps in Pochutla.
-If sky image doesn't exist, black blank image is now used (fixing dark underground maps on low draw distance).
-Added new script command: "setMainPlayer" (to change the main character of the game).
-Fixed crash when loading a new custom story file.

SCRIPTS:
-Fixed bug with banana beer not leaving behind tin cans.
-Hounds are now removed from party in Chapter 2 to prevent repeated message bug.
-Fixed bug in which selling pearls got you UBNS respect even if you're working for Eleggua.
-Fixed bug where silencing a Crow 10mm increased ammo capacity.
-Laughing Coyote now says "Chaos is Restless" much less often.
-Rains Through Roof now surrenders after UBNS takes the city.
-Fixed a couple of bugs with missing sound files.
-Fixed final scores, making it one point harder.

RESOURCES:

-Added new ambient sound for inside oil platform: "ambMachine.wav".

STORY FILE: (requires starting a new game)

-Made some stools in corners of houses normal (not passable) so they can be used as tables.
-Fixed bug that would get you stuck in river between Pochutla Market and South of Pochutla.
-Reworked some rocks in the Ancient Ruins so that player can't reach the wrong cave entrance.
-Made it impossible to jump the south wall of Pochutla, added some goodies for trying.

notes.title: Still Alive
notes.content:
Can't update as much because I am working on the Panama DLC. It's gonna be half the length of the original, with lots of new items, abilities, baddies, and characters.

I don't know if I should release the demo, as it will contain spoilers. Maybe instead just to satiate potential customer appetites I will release another challenge map with no story.

notes.title: Version 4.0
notes.content:
Whooo! I finally fixed the bug that caused your Strength skill to drop. It was the Power Strike ability that was causing it, and it took me way too long to figure out. I fixed the bug that caused Ricardo's dialogue to reset. I also fixed problems with the following abilities: Power Strike, Sneak Attack, and Night Prowler.

There are a bunch of other minor fixes. I was planning to have some big aesthetic overhaul for version 4, but oh well. I think that pretty much torches all the bugs and hopefully their larvae as well, so I wanted to upload this patch ASAP.

Now I just need to work on those reported performance issues, and that memory issue where it crashes on some computers after loading too many maps. The quick solution to that is to exit the game and load it again after you visit about 5 maps in one session. I could probably fix this memory issue, but I need access to a computer that has this problem first.

EDIT: The performance issue and the memory crash issue are unrelated.

notes.title: Minor Update
notes.content:
I fixed a problem with bullet hit sounds (on metal, etc.), fixed another BSL script command, and increased SIMDA relay durability from 60 to 100 to make the defense easier. Starting now I'm gonna just be working on Brigand: Panama, which may take another couple of months.

If anybody can help me with the following reported bugs that I have not been able to recreate and give me some more details, it would be much appreciated:

-Random changes to the Strength skill??? (most important, can't recreate it)
-Ricardo's dialogue resetting after the first couple chapters (not game-breaking)
-Hidden character limbs sometimes reappearing (like default AKs for thugs, etc., though I think this bug has been fixed).

I'm just gonna work on Panama DLC for now unless someone gives me some more info on the above reported bugs. Thanks.

notes.title: New Patch on Friday (or Saturday)
notes.content:
There are some new bug reports (and some old complaints) that I'll try to fix before Saturday. There are probably some new script problems that arose after I changed the assets folder system for modability.

Also there are some slowdown and crashing issues on some computers. The low FPS and crashing problems are unrelated, but I'll work on both of them.

EDIT: The game will crash on some computers if you load too many maps (and hence images) in one play session without quitting. So the temporary solution is to quit and reopen the game after you save to prevent crashes. Most computers don't have this problem, but I'll try to fix it in the next patch (or the one after).

notes.title: More Panama Progress
notes.content:
Quick update since I haven't posted in a couple weeks. I've been working on the story for Brigand: Panama, as well as the world editor. I can design a map in no time now with these new functions and editing scripts. Here are some screenshots of maps in progress for the Panama DLC. The planned release date is early October, but I'll probably include a demo with the next update in a week or two.

The plot of Brigand: Panama will be a combination of Apocalypse Now and Scarface. The player arrives in Panama branded as an exile from the Pirate Kingdoms, and he must follow Ozee's crew south along the canal and stop them from uncovering abandoned Baroque Tribe technology from the jungle.

notes.title: Version 3.7, Framerate Increase
notes.content:
Yeeeaahh, I fixed the framerate slowdown on some computers, I think. I was playtesting on high game speed (46 FPS), and noticed the game slowed way down when walking on ground or cliff terrain on crowded maps. This has been fixed, so everything should be much smoother now.

I also added a bunch of performance options before I made this discovery. You can now run the game in 16-bit color, turn down the draw distance, and turn down the rain effects (so that the rain completely stops when you are indoors, so there's no need for raindrop collision). But honestly you probably won't need these new options now that I fixed that aforementioned slowdown bug. I need your feedback with all your own computers and video cards.

Also some other minor bugs were fixed (check updates text).

notes.title: 1-Year Steam Anniversary
notes.content:
Whoo! It's been a year and two days and I made about $3000, which covers my annual weed budget plus a little booze, but starting July 1st marijuana prices almost doubled in California thanks to incompetent government fucks, so I need more money.

The release date for the Brigand: Panama DLC is September (sometime) and it should cost about $4.99 but it will only be about half the length. I apologize in advance for this, but it will have tons of new items, abilities, baddies, and traps. And I can use all the new features again in Brigand: High Seas (or Pirate Kingoms, can't decide), which will cost about $2.99 but it will just be a few highly-difficult challenge maps with minimal story. Let me know what you guys think.

Also, here is an interview about Brigand by author Patrick Hickey, Jr.

https://www.oldschoolgamermagazine.com/old-school-gamer-magazine-exclusive-inside-brigand-oaxaca/

notes.title: Version 3.6
notes.content:
The most important bug fix was that thrown items would not run their hit scripts if they were past their throw peak and falling (i.e. throwing a poison axe sometimes wouldn't poison your target). That's been fixed.

Poison Blade and Eleggua's Curse abilities now require a target, just like the Gun Smith ability, rather than bringing up a list. This is so I can add more weapons that you can poison/curse in the DLC. I also made it possible to curse plates, trays, cinder blocks, and microscopes (anything you can throw you can now curse). The cursed hit animations also look a bit better now.

I also fixed a couple of script oversights, improved some text, and prevented items from being thrown off the map. Here's a complete list.

SOURCE CODE:
-Fixed bug in which thrown items wouldn't run hit scripts if falling, after throwing peak.
-Improved weapon gluing to limbs for characters who are attacking a bit (still not perfect).
-Changing the volume option in the menu now instantly turns down environment sounds that are still playing.
-Prevented items from being thrown off the map (and getting out of reach).
-Decreased map AI range a bit (the last update made it a bit too slow).

SCRIPTS:
-Added new flavor text to Chapter 1 opening depending on the player's chosen class (speculations about why they framed you).
-Changed Poison Blade and Eleggua's Curse abilities to require a specific target for a weapon, rather than selecting from a list.
-Added the option to use Eleggua's Curse ability on plates, trays, microscopes, pipes, and cinder blocks (so they cause cold damage).
-Improved HIT script for cursed melee and thrown weapons, showing new animation and sound.
-Fixed bug in which you could only bring Ricardo a batch of coca leaves one time.
-Fixed bug in which UB Mercs would get bloody after one point of damage.
-Fixed some melee weapon INIT scripts to correct grip limb positions.
-Fixed Harbinger Sniper INIT script to fix a texture problem.

RESOURCES:
-Added cursed textures and icons for cinder blocks, plates, trays, pipes, and microscopes.
-Removed more duplicate objects from the OAXACA assets folder, making the total file size smaller.
-Made the toilet flushing sound quieter.
-Improved a couple of textures.

STORY FILE: (requires starting a new game)
-Fixed Harbinger Sniper drawing priority in story files (to fix texture).
-Fixed some melee weapon grip limb positions in the story files.

notes.title: Sale Tomorrow, Also DLC Progress
notes.content:
Another sale starts tomorrow so I can get my shit promoted, essentially, so you can save $2 to spend on... something.

So far I've made about 6 new characters for the DLC, and I'm working on new items, abilities, and baddies as well. I don't wanna give away the shit from the end of the story, but I will gladly tell you about stuff from the beginning of the story.

There will be rum, oysters, bamboo, and a Woodcraft ability (Hardware) that lets you make spears, fishing rods, blowguns, and darts. Also there will be a lot of traps. Later shit I wanna keep quiet.

notes.title: Version 3.5
notes.content:
Fixed a bug where the player wouldn't automatically obtain coins from corpses if there's another item sitting on top of it, so now it should be easier to make some more money. Also, I deleted a lot more duplicate assets. The total file size is down to under 800 megs now. Lots of other little fixes, so look at the Updates txt for a complete list, as always.

I've started working on the Panama DLC. I've made a few new character skins and I have a bunch of new objects, but I don't wanna give anything away this early. It will still be a couple of months before it's finished.

notes.title: Brigand: Panama
notes.content: Would you guys pay $3.99 for a 3-chapter DLC story in Panama? There will be new weapons and items. There will also be new enemies, but really just retextures of old enemies, but they will have new abilities.

notes.title: Version 3.4B + Future Plans
notes.content:
I just did a quick update to fix a couple of bugs, one where all the Subz Juicers would disappear in the Scumlands before the player can fight them, and another one where the wrong Chapter 2 loading screen shows up (there are two completely different second chapters). Also, I added a unique face icon for Fluffy the dog.

There's gonna be another patch before the end of the month, not sure when. I'm making the world editor easier to use, not for you people, but so I can encourage myself to make a bit of new content without wasting so much time. Might as well, since I spent so long making this game highly mod-able.

If there are any more suggestions or bugs, please let me know.

notes.title: Version 3.4
notes.content:
Major update with 3.4. I redesigned the entire Assets folder so that game stories will look for the assets in the special story folder first, then look in the default folder as an alternative. This means that I deleted a lot of duplicate files so the game is now less than a gig, and also it will be easier to make new stories (you don't have to copy the entire default assets folder anymore). This should encourage me to make another challenge map some time in the near future. The next update will include more world editor improvements.

I also fixed a problem with the last update that slowed the player down when moving on terrain, and I made enemies' heads explode with enough damage on a head shot.

Another important change is that I gave more Voodoo skill to the Witchdoctor class (but less Willpower). This is because it's hard to find a Voodoo trainer early in the game.

Here's a complete list of fixes:

SOURCE CODE:
-Redesigned asset folders so that story folder takes priority, other use default folder (eliminating the need for duplicate files).
-Fixed bug from the last update which caused the player to move more slowly on the ground terrain matrix.
-Fixed bug in which muting volume in game launcher would disable map loading music, even after turning volume back on.
-Fixed a rare bug in which teammates would transfer to map with player but leave the team.
-The "NewStory" command now gives you the option of creating a new empty assets folder.
-Targets' heads now explode if dealt enough damage and killed in a head shot.
-Decreased slope speed penalties, especially moving downhill.
-Decreased cliff sliding damage, increased free fall damage.

SCRIPTS:
-Fixed bug where Carmen would still teleport outside the Polyphonic if the entire team leaves.
-Fixed bug in which beers would sometimes leave you with another beer instead of an empty can (though the texture would change).
-Fixed bug in finale in which McVannon would talk to you prematurely while you're on the top floor.
-Fixed bug where one of the backup rowboats on the oil platform spawns sticking through a wall.
-Decreased Witchdoctor starting Willpower from 30 to 25 and increased Voodoo from 10 to 15.
-Added one final isopod demon respawn on Freeway 200 in Chapter 10.
-Gave Gao 10 Pistols skill because he starts with a pistol (init script).
-Increased Zac's Voodoo from 10 to 20 for player training (init script).
-Made Cortez's initial dialogue exit automatically in BRIGAND - FORTRESS.

RESOURCES:
-Eliminated most duplicate asset files, greatly reducing file size.
-Improved textures: "plaster" and "plasterB" (starting cell).
-Added nighttime cliff and ground textures for map corners.
-Updated Brigand Builder's Manual.

STORY FILE: (requires starting a new game)
-Changed texture of loose dirt in the Scumlands so it's not the same as the ground texture.
-Gave Gao 10 Pistols skill because he starts with a pistol (story file).
-Increased Zac's Voodoo from 10 to 20 for player training (story file).
-Improved Freeway 175 map a bit.

notes.title: Version 3.3
notes.content:
Oops, I forgot to add 1920x1080 hi-res scope zooms, etc. to the assets folder. That's now fixed, as well as a ton of other stuff.

I added new information to the character screen, showing weapon damage, accuracy, and delay (which are affected by the weapon stats, condition, and the character's skills). After implementing this, I noticed that every single Vulture 44 pistol in the game used the Rifles skill instead of the Pistols skill. Oops again. Don't know why I didn't notice that before. Fixed now.

I also fixed a bug where character textures would be bloodied up after taking just 1 damage. Now the textures get bloodied up when they are below half health.

Here's a complete list of fixes:

SOURCE CODE:
-Fixed "if_healthper" script command so that character textures don't get bloodied up after 1 damage.
-Added weapon accuracy, damage, and delay statistics to the character screen, determined by both skill and weapon stats.
-Increased listener scale from 0.5 to 0.6 (sounds are now louder).
-Added 1920x1080 resolution scope zoom and screen overlays.

notes.title: Version 2.9

-Prevented McVannon from yelling taunts in finale until you talk to him first.
-Added a couple more chapter respawns of thugs, mercs, and demons.
-Increased Tesla weapon damage from 16 to 20 (init scripts).
-Increased Android Vitality from 30 to 40 (init scripts).

RESOURCES:
-Added new anim: images\anims\fire2Die.bmp
-Added new anim: images\anims\gasDie.bmp

STORY FILE: (requires starting a new game)
-Made Noise of Running Feet a little taller.
-Made merc by plantation bridge stand ground (so he doesn't go swimming).
-Increased Tesla weapon damage from 16 to 20 (game files).
-Increased Android Vitality from 30 to 40 (game files).

notes.title: Version 2.8
notes.content:
Version 2.8 of Brigand is up, which makes the game a little easier. There are more save points and helpful items, but only if you start a new game. Also, I fixed a bug that prevented the player from scoring head shots. The player can now score head shots on almost all baddies, doubling the damage -- don't worry, ONLY the player can score head shots. I also fixed a bug that prevented teammates from reloading their gun if they had a melee weapon. Finally, I increased the damage of the Shorty AR and the Harbinger Sniper, just because they are so expensive. These things will make the game slightly easier, because I do want a few more people to beat it.

I also improved the GUI of the world editor a bit and allowed quick saving when using the world editor mode (F3). That means if you REALLY want to save scum, play the world editor mode and press F3 to save at any time (you no longer need to type any commands). Also, there are some small aesthetic improvements, as well as a compass object that you must now use to activate the HUD compass. The compass is easy to find.

There are still 3 known bugs that I can't seem to fix, but they are very rare and minor. Hopefully the next update will fix all known issues once and for all. You can check out the update text in the game folder for more info.

notes.title: Version 2.7
notes.content:
Major update, added 1600x900 resolution, better blood effects, made enemies drop laser weapons after they are empty to make the game slightly less frustrating. Most importantly, I fixed that damn bug when a baddie is swimming under the docks in Loma Larga getting stuck on the posts and slowing down the entire map. I'll just post the update txt:

SOURCE CODE:
-Added support for 1600x900 resolution.
-Removed hi-res menu backgrounds and added a default frame around low-res backgrounds instead.
-Fixed bug in which baddies would get stuck under the docks in Loma Larga and the game would slow down significantly.
-Fixed bug in which player would only be able to recover one of any stacked inventory item after being abducted by Baroque Tribe.
-Fixed bug in world editor which snapped items to integer values when using the move commands (xmove, ymove, zmove).
-Coins are now automatically obtained (if object tag is "coin").

SCRIPTS:
-Changed laser reload scripts, causing AI to drop them and equip a katana instead (making the game a little easier).
-Updated assassin spawn scripts to make sure every assassin has a katana for when they run out of laser charges.
-Removed redundant text from the descriptions of cyber assassins and Pluto (shown when player uses the Analyze Opponent ability).
-Updated damage scripts to add more bloodied texture variety.
-Neuro Demons are now immune to fear.

RESOURCES:
-Removed hi-res menu backgrounds and improved some HUD images (including scope zoom).
-Added more bloodied character textures for variety.

STORY FILE: (requires starting a new game)
-Improved aesthetics on Ricardo's Plantation a bit and gave Jimmy the Barkeep a weapon.
-Added a save point shelter to the Oaxacan Jungle map, near the transition to the Ancient Ruins.
-Gave katanas (some poison) to all assassins, even the ones with lasers (because enemies can no longer reload lasers).

Now for some victory music:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nffKT1m8_Fk&list=PLE93E9018751C4A86&index=20

notes.title: Version 2.6
notes.content:
I never got around to fixing that slow-down problem if there's a baddie under the docks trying to kill you in Loma Larga (next time), but I did make a few significant improvements.

Most importantly, when a character dies, their items will scatter a little bit to make each item easier to target. Coins are spawned in the death script, though, so they will still all be in the same place. When I watch people playing on Youtube, though, it seems like they are still trying to target items through corpses. You don't have to target something if it's at your feet, just look at the "(on ground)" description at the top of the screen and right click if you are not targeting anything else.

I also made the blood splatters look a little bit better, which is arguably more important than actual gameplay. The variety of blood splatter animations is now doubled, and they are easier to see.

There are some other minor fixes. Next time I will fix that Loma Larga slowdown bug. But for now if you are in Loma Larga and the game is running slow, that means you gotta drop down below the docks and kill a demon stuck down there. New patch in 2 weeks (total guess).

notes.title: Version 2.5
notes.content:
I guess I have made enough fixes and improvements to release a new patch, but I didn't do everything I wanted. I fixed lots of bugs reported by thegametuber and a couple from Alex, who does the Youtube Let's Play. You can look at the updates text file for a complete list, but since there were a few important things I didn't get to, I'll just list those unfinished issues here. They will all be fixed in the next patch in a week or two.

1) Firstly, looting corpses can still be annoying. I need to think more about the mechanics of looting corpses. I guess I can scatter the items a bit, but I want to make sure it all works before throwing that crap online.

2) Next, I noticed that the game slows way down when baddies are swimming in the water under the docks in Loma Larga. I'm still not sure why, but there are definitely still some slow-down issues related to AI.

3) The other big issue is that sometimes baddies will drop items that are unobtainable, but this is extremely rare I think and it never breaks the game.

(Damn, I wanna start on a new project, but this horse's corpse has not yet been beaten enough. I still have to piss on it a bit.)

notes.title: Version 2.4
notes.content:
I was planning to wait until January for the next version, but a couple of issues required immediate attention. There was a game-breaking bug in Chapter 8 found by Hedoroman1. Thankfully he plays through the game 10x faster than the average pleb (he's beaten it twice now). I also noticed that the game got really slow in the Topo Tracks due to an AI problem that has now been fixed. I think the entire game should run a bit more smoothly now.

I also fixed a script bug in the new Fortress story file in which the twilight skybox would persist all night instead of changing to the night skybox.

In addition to these bug fixes, I added a new feature which makes demon biomass objects with material set to "animal" pulsate like a living organism, hopefully adding a bit of disgusting flavor to the game. Also, I added a new end-game screen describing the fate of Junk Fort and the plantation.

Finally, there are some new keywords for the "Ask" feature that is present in some dialogue trees.

As always, you can look at the Updates text file for a complete list.

notes.title: Version 2.3
notes.content:
A small but important update is up. It fixes some script bugs pointed out by Elkinda, most importantly the bug in which Voodoo Altars would not work, preventing you from sacrificing gold to cure your insanity and making Voodoo essentially useless. Some dialogue bugs have also been fixed. Finally, I also fixed a corrupt voice sound file that crashed the game, pointed out by Hedoroman1.

The next update will be out in January with more substantial improvements. I will try to improve some textures and add some more details to the maps.

There is a still a bug in which hidden object limbs sometimes reappear (like the default AKs held by thugs, which should not be visible at all). Other than this bug, I think everything else is fixed in the main game, but I'm sure the world editor still has some issues.

For some reason I decided that the official campaign story file needed its own special assets folder and that the new single-map story would use the "Default" assets folder because the scripts, etc. are much simpler.

notes.title: Version 2.2 + New DLC
notes.content:
Version 2.2 is up, along with the new DLC I promised so long ago. It's not really DLC, since it's included with the game now. This is because I want an example alternative story file so people can learn how the world editor works.

Just start a new game and choose the new story file, BRIGAND - FORTRESS.

It is only one map in which you must defend a SIMDA relay for 3 days and 3 nights (one hour in real time). When the baddies are attacking, you can complete side jobs, hire muscle to help you out, activate automated security systems, scavenge for items, and explore the area for vantage points.

This is meant to be a possible demo for a future paid DLC called Brigand: Panama, but it will be quite a while before that comes out, and also I need some people to help me with new character textures. Thanks to Unmutual for helping me out with the texture for Officer Cortez.

Warning: the third and final night is extremely hard.

notes.title: Two More Days
notes.content:
This time I swear that the new free DLC and new version will be out on Tuesday night. Both will come together, at the same time, as nature intended. Just one map, defending a SIMDA relay outside a jungle fort for 3 days and 3 nights against both demons and enemy human tribes. You can hire more mercs to help your defense, go scavenge for supplies between attack waves, and reactivate automatic security systems. You will get more jink and points to spend to help you defend the relay. I'm still working on a couple of side jobs, making the dialogue better, and testing the difficulty.

notes.title: Plans for the Future
notes.content:
I'm gonna start working on the free challenge story this week, and it should be ready next Sunday for download. I will also be making updates to the world editor, making it prettier and more user-friendly.

As for the main story and game engine, I'll wait for more bug reports and general suggestions before releasing another update. I was thinking about adding mini-health bars to all the teammate portraits and putting some more details into the maps. Also, I want to correct the corpse angles so dead people don't stick through walls when they are on the ground. Otherwise I think the main story and game engine are done.

The long-term goal is to make a paid DLC for maybe $2.99. It will be a totally new story, about half as long as the main story. I already have a bunch of new assets and ideas for weapons, bosses, etc., but I don't know if it should take place in Panama or Cuba. I am still open to suggestions before I start really planning.

notes.title: Version 2.0
notes.content:
I finally got the new version up and everything seems to be working. I would back up your save file if you have one, though, as the sub-directories have all changed to accommodate for multiple story files. It's probably fine, but better to be safe.

Included is a save converter, so if you want to continue your character from version 1, run that program first on the launch menu, select your character, and wait a few seconds.

Major changes include a new World Editor launch option. The world editor could still use some work, but you can play around with it and start creating your own stories. I still have to implement a way to upload files, but it will probably be a while before any content is ready anyway. I was planning to have a free example DLC story with this release, but that will have to wait a week or so. It will be a single-map defense challenge.

As for bug fixes, the upside-down texture bug is no more. The solution was so simple that I now spit at my reflection in the mirror every morning for not fixing it earlier. I also increased the max objects per map from 2000 to 5000, so feel free to hoard as many guns and beers as you want on any map -- it won't crash the game.

There's a whole lot of other fixes, too. Check the Brigand Updates text file in the game folder to see everything that's been updated.

notes.title: v2.0 Progress Report
notes.content:
So some good news: I fixed the upside-down texture bug! Whoo! I also increased the max objects per map, as well as the max frame rate. This will all be included in 2.0 on Halloween.

What I am doing now is perfecting the world editor. The most important thing is that I'm dividing the assets (objects, images, sounds, music, and scripts) into separate folders for each story file. This will mean that each new DLC story file will have to have duplicate copies of the default resources if it's gonna use them, taking up more hard disk space. It sounds counter-intuitive, but allow me to explain.

I got really into user-generated content for Neverwinter Nights 1 back in the day. Lots of that stuff was far superior to the official campaign, and that's what I'm hoping for here as well. Unfortunately, downloading some user-generated mods used to fuck with other user-generated mods in NWN, which is what I am hoping to avoid here. I want each downloadable story file to have its own assets folder, so that it will not fuck with the assets of another story file. That means more hard disk space, but less confusion and irritation, hopefully.

I'm also trying to make the World Editor and Builder's Manual as clear and user-friendly as possible. It should all be ready in two weeks. Thanks to all the users here on Steam that reported bugs and suggestions. Without you bastards, I would still be lost on itch.io somewhere with no customers.

notes.title: Plans for 2.0 (release: Halloween)
notes.content:
I've been busy with real life lately, but I will start work on v2.0 this weekend and hopefully finish by the end of October. Here is a list of the planned improvements, but I am always open to more suggestions:

1) Most importantly, there will be a new World Editor launch app, which will be like the main low-res game app, but it will allow you to open two editor modes: GUI and a command prompt. You can edit anything while you play, including maps, dialogue scripts, AI, etc. You can also erase the entire game and build your own story from scratch, importing any models you want. You can then save your new story file for others to download and play.

2) The max number of objects per map will be increased from 2000 to 5000. The game currently crashes if the player hoards too many items on one map. This improvement will require larger save files, so old saves will not be compatible.

3) A few new menu options, including one to increase the frame rate from 33 to 66. These new menu options are another reason old saves will not be compatible.

4) Hopefully I will fix the bug where textures flip upside-down. I have a new version of the compiler which fixes it, but it doubles the loading times and causes a couple other problems, so I may just add another launch option if I can't fix it in the current compiler version.

5) There will be bloodstained textures for injured characters.

6) A simple challenge story file to demonstrate the World Editor functionality.

Please give me more suggestions. I can't promise they will be implemented by Halloween, but I can try.

notes.title: Version 1.9B
notes.content:
This will be the last update before 2.0. When 2.0 gets released your previous saves will not work. I need to increase the max objects per map, and add more options in the settings, which means I need more variables in the save files. And when the max objects increase I will add a lot more details on the maps.

The main fix in 1.9B is that I changed the auto-pickup system. Now you just automatically target items at your feet, and you can right click to pick it up. This will make the game harder for sure when you are running around a battlefield looting corpses, but it is much less annoying. Please let me know what you think.

There have of course been other fixes, check Brigand Updates.txt.

EDIT: I will definitely leave the old version up when 2.0 comes out so people can finish their games.

notes.title: Version 1.9
notes.content:
I decided to release the next version early, even though I haven't resolved the updside-down texture bug yet. I am still waiting to use a computer that has this bug on it.

Things I did add, however, include a compass pointing north. Since people give you cardinal directions in the dialogue, there should be a compass in the HUD.

There are also many other script fixes that you can see in the Updates text file. The Eyes of the Beast spell now works, letting you control hounds and demons, and the Control Android function on terminals now works as well. There are also some more script fixes for side objectives.

I should have a 1.9B out as soon as I fix the upside-down textures. Then I'm gonna take a break for a couple weeks before 2.0, which will include the world editor and a sample DLC challenge.

Unfortunately, I need to increase the max objects per map. I forgot about digital hoarders who like to collect every banana in the game and stash them in their abode. In order to increase the max objects, I will have to change the saving source code, which means old saves will not be compatible with 2.0. That is still a few weeks away, though, and I think the main story file is pretty much bug-free.

There are also many other script fixes that you can see in the Updates text file. The Eyes of the Beast spell now works, letting you control hounds and demons, and the Control Android function on terminals now works as well. There are also some more script fixes for side objectives.

I should have a 1.9B out as soon as I fix the upside-down textures. Then I'm gonna take a break for a couple weeks before 2.0, which will include the world editor and a sample DLC challenge.

Unfortunately, I need to increase the max objects per map. I forgot about digital hoarders who like to collect every banana in the game and stash them in their abode. In order to increase the max objects, I will have to change the saving source code, which means old saves will not be compatible with 2.0. That is still a few weeks away, though, and I think the main story file is pretty much bug-free.

notes.title: Demo Is Up
notes.content:
The demo is finally up on Steam. You can find the demo button on the Store Page.

Version 1.7 will be up on Sunday evening. Again, it's mostly just bug fixes. They have been ably pointed out to me by someone named Miran by email, but I'm not sure who it is on Steam. Anyway, Miran has recently beaten the game and sent me pages of bug reports I never would have found by myself.

These bug-fixes are mostly script-related, as in they are in the separate script files that can be easily edited with notepad. Scripts don't require you to compile anything, and they contain everything from dialogue trees to object properties, character AI, day/night cycles, skills and abilities, status effects, and more. I have a Builder's Manual ready to be released with the world editor that explains how to make/alter scripts, etc.

First, however, I need to make sure the main story is bug-free, and there is much to be fixed.

The demo seems to be perfectly fine, though. It is only the first 2 maps out of 21, so there is not too much story to get twisted up in the scripts.

Thanks again for all the playtesters. If you want your name/website in the credits, just send me a message.

notes.title: Need Help With Bug Testing
notes.content:
I'm gonna release a new version in a couple hours here, but that inexplicable bug in which some textures (notably signs) flip upside-down at night on some computers may not be fixed. I cannot find a computer to use that has this bug. I do have a theory, however, involving file types.

For textures, the game can use BMPs (if you need black-pixel transparency), PNGs (which are the fastest common images to load as textures), and DDS (which are even faster than PNG and harder to rip off).

For object files, the game can use .X objects, but I converted them to .DBO (which again, are slightly faster to load in DarkBASIC and also harder to rip off).

For the upcoming version, 1.6, I have replaced the files for the sign and the apartment building with the original .X files. I need your help to see if the upside-down textures are fixed. If not, I'll try the image files next.

I'll upload the new version in a couple hours. Thanks.

notes.title: Version 1.2
notes.content:
Just put up the second update, fixing lots of script bugs that prevented some side objectives from being completed, thanks to Hedoroman1, who has been blasting through the game faster than I ever thought possible. There was also one corrupt voice file which crashed the game in Chapter 8, which is now fixed.

Finally, I think the problem with dual monitors is fixed. The cursor used to cross over to the other monitor, which also made the game unplayable. I do not have dual monitors to test this, but I think it's fixed. Please let me know, all your nerds with dual monitors.
